sentences.text: ORDER Heard Sri Santosh Patil, learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt. Maya T.R., learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State.

2. The present petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., with the following prayer:
"Therefore, it is most humbly prayed to the Hon'ble Court to release the petitioner on bail in Crime No. 119/2022 of Nimbarga Police Station, Dist. Kalaburagi, for the offences punishable U/sec. 498-A, 306 r/w sec. 34 of IPC pending before the Prl.
Civil Judge (J.D.) and J.M.F.C. at Aland."

3. Brief facts which are necessary for disposal of the present petition are as under:
A complaint came to be filed by Kalyani S/o Ramanna Jogan, whereby Nimbarga Police have registered a case in Crime No.119/2022 on 07.12.2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 306 read with section 34 of IPC.
4.
Gist of the complaint averments reveal that Shivamma being the daughter of the complainant was married to accused No.1-Mahesh Shreemant Kadaganchi.
After marrying about a year, Shivamma led a happy married life in the matrimonial house.
Later she was harassed physically and mentally on the ground that she is not good looking and she does not know how to cook food.
The elders of the family convened a panchayat wherein son-in-law and his parents were advised to look after Shivamma in proper manner.
Despite such an advice, the harassment continued.

5. When the matter stood thus, on 05.12.2022 at about 10.30 a.m., petitioner locked the house from outside after pulling Shivamma out of the house and told her that her son has gone out of the house and she should join him.
The deceased telephoned to the son of the complainant and intimated him.
However, she was advised to stay in the matrimonial house.

2 6.

When the matter stood thus, at about 2.30 pm., on 06.12.2022, when complainant and his wife and others were having lunch, at that juncture, one Sachin came to the house of complainant and intimated that Shivamma fell into a well and committed suicide and the dead body is floating in the well.
Immediately, she was shifted to the hospital.
Thereafter, they have approached the police and lodged a complaint.

Police are investigating the matter, inter alia, arrested the petitioner on 07.12.2022.
7.
The attempt made by the petitioner for grant of bail is turned down by the learned District and Sessions Judge by order dated 06.01.2023 in Crl. Misc. No.2556/2022.
Thereafter, the petitioner is before this Court.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioner reiterating the grounds urged in the bail petition vehemently contended that petitioner being the lady and she is in custody since 07.12.2022 and having regard to the nature of offence alleged against the petitioner, continuation of the petitioner in judicial custody is no longer warranted and sought for grant of bail.

9. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the bail petition on the ground that it is the petitioner who is directly responsible for suicidal death of Shivamma inasmuch as it is she who told Shivamma to quit the matrimonial house as the petitioner's son had gone somewhere else and she is required to join her son and not to live in the matrimonial house resulting in frustration in the mind of deceased, which has resulted in suicide by Shivamma and sought for rejection of the bail.
10. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
11. On such perusal of the material on record, it is seen that the incident has occurred on 06.12.2022 and on 07.12.2022 complaint came to be lodged and immediately petitioner is arrested.
12. Even assuming that the entire allegations in the complaint is accepted as true for the sake of arguments, the continuation of the accused in judicial custody is no longer warranted.

Moreover,
accused/petitioner is a lady.
13. It is not a case where custodial trial is utmost necessary.

Having regard to the fact that accused is in custody on and from 07.12.2022 and charge sheet is about to be filed, this Court is of the considered opinion, that the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail.

14. Suffice to say that apprehension of the prosecution can be met with by imposing suitable and stringent conditions.
15.
Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.
